category_title: Struggling readers who directly refuse to read
minimal_context: The student and interventionist are participating in a one-on-one shared reading session using the book 'Miss Nelson is missing!'.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's continue our shared reading of 'Miss Nelson is missing!'.

STUDENT: (Makes a reading attempt)

TUTOR: That did not make sense.

STUDENT: (Slumps back in chair with frown)

TUTOR: You wanta start this page?

STUDENT: (whispered) No.

options.A: Continuously remind the student that they are expected to show they are participating, even if they are not completely comfortable with the reading.
options.B: Provide written feedback using a 3-point Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (needs improvement) to 3 (great job) at the end of each shared reading session.
options.C: Ask lower-level questions focused primarily on having the student recall additional factual information about the characters, setting, or plot of the book.
options.D: Treat the student's avoidance strategies as compensations rather than refusals to comply with the expected reading task.
